title: RFC: Move forums to GitHub Discussions
body:
The forums continue to run well on phpbb and I am hesitant to mess with something that is working, but there are definitely a few things I'd like to improve. We looked at migrating to Discourse, which I think would be an overall improvement over phpbb, but recently GitHub have added "Discussions" support, and I think this might be a better direction.

- Keep everything in one place (GitHub) for code, issues, PRs, and now discussion.
- Much more modern editing (including emoji response, threads, accepted answer, etc) and markup tools (code formatting, etc).
- Many users already have GitHub accounts, whereas current creating a forum.micropython.org account is an extra step (also it's not possible for new users to create new threads on the existing forum until they reply to some other threads).
- Better support for notifications and subscriptions.
- Don't need to run/maintain our own server.

The modern editing/markup tools are a big factor for me. It may sound a bit trivial but the emoji response would be really nice just to judge engagement, and the accepted answer feature would make it easier for people to make use of previous threads. There's also category support (just like phpbb) but also tagging.

Downsides:
 - There's no automatic way to import history, so we'd need to leave the current forum running in read-only mode. (FWIW, this was also an issue with moving to Discourse, there's a phpbb importer but it had issues). There is a huge wealth of information in the forums. (It looks like it _should_ be possible to use the GitHub API to import thread content, although all the posts would be from a robot account but we could annotate the message text with the original author).
 - No way to import users, so people would need to create GitHub accounts to post/reply (this is really no different to the current forum, so this really only impacts the (small number of?) people who have forum accounts but not GitHub accounts).
 - More dependence on a third-party service (GitHub).

Here's some example projects currently using GitHub notifications:

- https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/discussions/
- https://github.com/nodejs/node/discussions
- https://github.com/faster-cpython/ideas/discussions

More info here: https://docs.github.com/en/discussions

I propose that we could create an [organisation-level discussion](https://github.blog/changelog/2022-04-12-organization-discussions/) (conceptually, spanning micropython and micropython-lib).

Keen to hear what people think! cc @participant11 @participant7 @davehylands @participant2 @kevinkk525 @participant10 @participant9 @scruss @projectgus (and @participant12 )

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I moved our forums from phpBB to Discourse a little over a year ago maybe, they did the migration for us (there was an option to do migration yourself, but I didn't want to risk it). It went really well, as I was told migration from phpBB is straightforward, and you get a chance to review everything before the handover. Also they offer different plans for hosting, so you don't have to worry about self-hosting either. Downside, it will cost more if you require more bandwidth, K-views/emails per month and storage etc... You should check phpBB stats first to determine which plan is needed and if it works with the current budget. FWIW we're on the standard plan (20 GB storage, 100k emails, and 100k pageviews per month) and it's more than enough for now. Overall, I'm very happy with the decision and it is definitely worth it.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
In the long run, I think the advantages outweigh the disadvantages. Let's say I'm +.5 :)

> The modern editing/markup tools are a big factor for me.

Yes having Markdown (or up, or whatever) looks minor but makes things much easier. It's simple, sane, very common, just works. Much better than having to enter `[code]` etc blocks.

> There is a huge wealth of information in the forums. (

There is, but: it's often almost inaccessible anyway. This was discussed briefly already, don't remember where; the only way to find something now is via search, and searching for common terms is going to turn up x useless posts whereas the couple of posts with golden info remain burried. Anyway this is common for all forums, the only solution I know of is a moderated list of sticky topics (in whatever form, could also be special tags).

That would probaby be my number one request: we cannot put everything in the docs anyway, a list of stickies per topic would be so good. Example: I'm pretty sure there are about 10 posts on memory 'leaks'/gc/finalizing created on the forum in the past years which are enough to answer basically any possible question on the topic, from high level to detailed. Time has gone into these posts, just being able to point other users to them would be a timesaver for everyone and just convenient overall.

> More dependence on a third-party service (GitHub)

I assume the API would always allow to pull all content out of it again?

> I propose that we could create an organisation-level discussion

Sounds good.

I have no experience with GitHub Discussions, am pretty happy with phpBB except for minor gripes like lack of inline-code markup (` `` ` in Markdown), and the few times I have used Discourse I just found it confusing.

They allow me to 1. read everything in one place in my newsreader, without having to check dozens of websites and 2. keep a local, offline-searchable archive. At a quick glance, GitHub Discussions doesn’t seem to have that, is that correct?

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
It appears you can move issues to discussions. That could eliminate all the "This is the bug tracker, this question would be better asked on the forum" by just bumping them to discussions.

You can create an issue from a discussion. This would allow discussion of potential bugs, eg is it a bug, a misunderstanding or deliberate limitation without cluttering the issue tracker and then create an issue from it if it is a bug or feature request. All the discussion history is copied into the issue.

RFCs might be better started in Discussions with a wider audience, then moved to issues when a consensus is nearer.

If you can search Discussions and Issues with the same search that might yield answers more quickly.

I think they are compelling reasons to use Discussions and would help keep the issue tracker clean.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
> It appears you can move issues to discussions.

Technically speaking you can't "move" the issue. You can "convert to a discussion" which means that the issue is copied to a new discussion and the issue is closed and locked but not removed or hidden.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
I believe we _must_ move away from phpbb. It's an impediment to get people involved - particularly for beginners - as the interface and markup and awkward to use. Further, it _looks_ old and dated, and I think it reflects poorly on MicroPython. These aren't just my opinions, I've heard it from _many_ people new to MicroPython.

Given that I think we need to move away from phpbb, Github Discussions is an _excellent_ replacement. It's modern, lightweight and the markup is sane (coloured syntax highlighting will be _very_ welcome!). I was advocating for Discourse before Discussions became available but Discussions is, generally, at least as good and better in many areas; such as the ease with referring to issues and PRs.

I'd be ok with making phpbb readonly and _not_ importing the history since it will be easily searchable if necessary. We'd need to figure out how to handle active discussions during the transition but that should be possible.

(I can imagine RSS may be a loss @participant3 - note that it is an open discussion: github-community/community/discussions/31)

So yes, +1, let's make it happen!

comments.author: participant14
comments.body:
I've worked with several different discussion platforms as part of my DevRel work, including content migrations. I've specifically supported a large high-volume Discourse community day-to-day for ~8 years. The past few years have seen a lot of projects move to Discourse and I'm pretty familiar with that - it's effective, and the trust levels can help with moderation (although can also be a barrier to entry sometimes). GH Discussions are a more recent entrant to the space but growing in popularity of course since a lot of activity happens alongside in Issues, Projects etc.

I really think it's time to move on from phpBB. As a relative newcomer to this community, I've engaged with the forums but I find it very difficult to see, at a glance, the most recent new topics or updates - I have to actively click into the categories. I've flirted with an RSS reader to keep up, but I just find myself not using the forums as much as I'd like. I imagine there are probably plugins to improve UX, but by default I don't find it great. Also phpBB markup / bbcode is something I constantly have to go lookup, but that's likely a familiarity thing now I mostly work in GfM... 

In general I'd support either Discourse or GH Discussions as a new home, and I'd be happy to help with a migration to either. I lightly lean towards GH Discussions since almost all of the project appears to be centered here, barring the website, docs, and wiki (and the latter lives in 2 or more places...)

One more thing to note is that there's absolutely a difference between forums, and chat - there exist multiple live chat platforms (Slack, Discord, IRC) but those conversations aren't kept in a searchable manner.

**Considerations / decision points**

- lifetime of the platform
  - per @participant12 comment in the meetup, ideally we want something that will last 10 years (which is more-or-less the life phpBB has served)
- how to manage history
  - can do an export/import for Discourse
  - could store an archive in GH, or leave the phpBB in place read-only (although then there's a challenge to encourage people to refer back / search for previous discussions in Yet Another Place)
- RSS / external access
  - Discourse ✅ and there's also an app
  - GH ❌ but there's also their app
- backup / future migration 
  - Discourse has export capability ✅ 
  - GH ❓ 
- moderation and access
  - Discourse has built-in education / get started, trust levels, and fine-grained roles, and it also enables you to set up different methods of sign-in outside of requiring a GH account
  - I'm yet to dig deeply on how much [control](https://docs.github.com/en/discussions/managing-discussions-for-your-community/moderating-discussions) GH Discussions provide, but I've seen a couple of projects deal with problematic discussion contributors so I know it's possible. I strongly agree with @participant7 that this is not something that should fall on the core maintainers. 

A final comment in favour of GH Discussions is that it would enable us to convert issues into discussions when appropriate, which may help with chipping away at the large number of existing issues.

On @participant12 comment about a new org-level repo - GitHub [does support this](https://docs.github.com/en/discussions/quickstart#enabling-github-discussions-on-your-organization). 

I'll go check the conversation on this same topic on phpBB as well 🙂 please count me in as someone to help with this work as needed.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
PSA: If anyone wants to filter out the discussions from issue/PR emails, there's unfortunately very little difference in the headers. It seems that the best option is to match the "repo-discussions" part of the message-id.

In GMail, you can't match on a partial message-id, however it seems to work to use `listid:micropython.micropython.github.com "repo-discussions"`.

i.e. I have
`listid:micropython.micropython.github.com -"repo-discussions"` --> archive, label `micropython`
`listid:micropython.micropython.github.com "repo-discussions"` --> archive, label `micropython/discussions`

Hopefully GitHub improve this... although see https://github.com/community/community/discussions/3021

comments.author: participant16
comments.body:
I'm obviously late to the party here, but I'm sad about the move to GH discussions. I have yet to run into a GH discussion forum where I am compelled to engage on a persistent manner. There are a number of discourse forums where I am active on an ongoing basis. I find the Gh discussion UI pretty awful and the way it works not conducive to forming sub-communities (e.g. folks interested in esp32, or rp2040, etc).

In particular, I find it very difficult to get a picture of what's going on. In a good forum there are categories and sub-categories, so for example I can go to the esp32 sub-category and quickly scroll through to see what has happened in the last couple of days/weeks. I know GH has tags but my experience is that tags proliferate and posts become inconsistent  in their tag usage. So filtering for the esp32 tag is not the same as going to an esp32 sub-category.

Gh discussions is also not great for seeing what's new. I read about reporter's method of using email, but my email is an even bigger disaster with way too many notifications from all kinds of stuff. I definitely do not want to add anything more to it!

In the end, a forum is about community and the tool needs to favor the creation of community and sub-community. I don't find that GH does that. IMHO Discourse is very good at that. If you have well-thought sub-categories you can get little communities of people who are interested in that category having lots of interesting discussions. I believe this happened for the various ports in the old forum too. It seems to be happening in discord too thanks to the hardware&ports channels. GH discussions is primarily a giant haystack of posts and finding gems in there is left as an exercise to the reader with some drop-downs for labels and filters. At least this is how it feels to me.

I also find the presentation on GH awful. I have a big monitor and the web browser full height yet, due to all the headers and side-bar I see only 11 posts, WFT? Makes it difficult to take a glance.

comments.body:
@reporter I think that If you even no have the MicroPython ports as categories, to have specific boards as categories will me a mess - because there are so many boards for each MicroPython port. In my opinion, firstly, starting creating all MicroPython ports as categories will be amazing.

MicroPython Ports as Categories: [esp32](https://micropython.org/download/?port=esp32), [esp8266](https://micropython.org/download/?port=esp8266), [mimxrt](https://micropython.org/download/?port=mimxrt), [nrf](https://micropython.org/download/?port=nrf), [renesas-ra](https://micropython.org/download/?port=renesas-ra), [rp2](https://micropython.org/download/?port=rp2), [samd](https://micropython.org/download/?port=samd), [stm32](https://micropython.org/download/?port=stm32) and so on.


On the MicroPython ports above (that will be categories), as soon the sub-category works on GH discussions, you can to create the specific boards (as sub-category) inside each MicroPython port.

In my opinion, for now (while subcategories feature still not working for all), more important than specific board as category, is to have firstly the all MicroPython ports as categories.
